lab.title: Who is on top, and can you trust it?
lab.intro: Every momentum chart hides a choice: how far back to look. Klupa shows three windows at once and tells you when the answer depends on that choice, or on a single chance.
lab.chartLabel: Chance balance over the last {{minutes}} minutes of half {{period}}. Above the line favours {{home}}, below favours {{away}}. Shots are marked above for {{home}} and below for {{away}}, sized by chance quality. The strip underneath shows what a coach may conclude at each moment; the table after the chart lists the time spent in each conclusion.
lab.stripLabel: Strip under the chart: what a coach may conclude at each moment. Drag across the chart to read any moment.
lab.tableCaption: Time spent in each conclusion this half
lab.explorerTitle: Try it on a professional match
lab.explorerIntro: Drag across the chart or use the slider. Each moment shows all three windows, the chances behind them and the one chance that carries the result.
lab.dataNote: Demo matches: DFL open event data with the provider's xG (CC BY 4.0). These are professional matches used to check the engine, not grassroots results.

research.title: What the research found
research.intro: Before you trust a momentum chart, see how often its windows disagree. Every number in this section is read straight from the research result files.
research.opposedLabel: 3- and 10-minute windows point at opposite teams
research.opposedHint: of the {{moments}} moments where both windows leaned one way
research.robustLabel: Agreed by every window and safe from one chance
research.robustHint: of all moments. Every window agreed at {{agreed}} of moments, but most of those agreements hang on a single chance.
research.byCompetitionNote: Share of moments where the 3- and 10-minute windows both lean and point at opposite teams.
research.byCompetitionLabel: Horizontal bar chart of the share of moments where the 3- and 10-minute windows point at opposite teams, by competition. All matches pooled: {{pooled}}. Earlier pilot: {{pilot}}. The table that follows lists every competition.
research.pilotNote: Our first pilot, on {{matches}} matches, found {{pilot}}: higher than the {{pooled}} across all matches. A handful of matches swings a lot. In {{draws}} random draws of {{matches}} matches from the large data, the pooled share fell between {{low}} and {{high}} in 95% of draws, and reached the pilot's value or more in {{tail}} of them. The pilot also used the provider's xG instead of our model, and we did not separate the two causes.
research.xgIntro: A logistic regression on shot distance, goal-mouth angle, header and free kick, trained on {{shots}} non-penalty shots ({{goals}} goals) from {{matches}} men's professional matches. The scores below come from {{folds}}-fold cross-validation grouped by match, so no match is in training and testing at once.
research.metricsCaption: Our expected-goals model against the base rate, cross-validated by match
research.metricsNote: Log loss and Brier: lower is better. AUC: 0.5 is guessing, 1 is perfect. The base rate gives every shot the same chance.
research.reliabilityLabel: Reliability chart: the mean predicted chance against the observed goal rate in {{bins}} bins with an equal number of shots. Points on the dashed diagonal are perfectly calibrated. Expected calibration error {{ece}}. The table that follows lists every bin.
research.limits: Limits. The model was trained on men's professional shots. No published study tests whether such a model transfers to youth football, and we have not tested it either: pitch, goals, ball and goalkeepers all differ. For youth teams, read it as a chance-quality index that ranks chances, not as a probability of scoring.
research.rejected: A momentum forecaster: does knowing which team leads on chance quality help predict the next shot? It did not. In a leave-one-match-out test, a simple recency baseline scored a log loss of {{recency}}; adding the chance-quality leader made it worse, {{withLeader}} (lower is better). We did not ship it, and Klupa makes no predictions.

source.dfl: DFL open event data: Bassek et al. 2025, CC BY 4.0 (demo matches)
source.wyscout: Wyscout open data: Pappalardo et al. 2019, CC BY 4.0 (large-scale study and xG training)

insufficient.label: Not enough evidence
insufficient.explain: No chances were recorded in the last 10 minutes. There is nothing to conclude.

level.label: Level
level.explain: Chances were recorded, but no window favours either team.

window-sensitive.label: Depends on the window
window-sensitive.explain: Not every window sees an advantage. Whether anyone is on top depends on how far back you look.
window-sensitive.explainOpposed: The windows favour opposite teams. Who is on top depends on how far back you look.

event-sensitive.label: Depends on one chance
event-sensitive.explain: All three windows favour {{side}}, but take away a single chance and that changes.

stable.label: Stable
stable.explain: All three windows favour {{side}}, and no single chance can change that.

reading.title: At {{time}}
reading.robust: Holds if any one chance is removed
reading.canTie: One chance fewer and it is level
reading.canReverse: One chance fewer and it flips
